items.title: Clarence Gabriel Interview
items.q: And one of the gentlemen, he called Kaiser, he told him, he said, man, you play so swell on that accordion.

ctx.x: My father. What did your father play? He played trumpet. Oh, he played trumpet. He had the national office. The national? National office. No, no. Y'all don't have no pictures of it around here? No. I don't believe they're taking any pictures of it in the mids, you know. I don't believe they're taking them. Can you tell us anything more about your father? Going back to your father for a little while, can you tell us, do you know where he learned to play the trumpet? Well, he did. He started around a place called…

Seems like I heard of a man by the name of Kaiser that had a place they called the pig ankle or something where they'd kick the ham and all that. That's right. That's right. Absolutely. Down there in the district, near the 25. That's correct. Run by Kaiser. That's correct.
